result:
Compiles cleanly on the first try.

I wrote `tests/org/apache/commons/lang3/reflect/MethodUtilsAgentTest.java`, a self-contained JUnit 5 test class covering `MethodUtils`:

- `getAccessibleMethod` (2-arg, 1-arg, name-based): finds methods via public interfaces, returns `null` when no accessible equivalent exists or on null inputs.
- `getAnnotation`: direct presence, absence, `searchSupers` behavior, NPE on null args.
- `getMatchingAccessibleMethod` / `getMatchingMethod`: primitive-wrapper matching, no-match `null`, ambiguous-match `IllegalStateException`, NPE on null class.
- `getMethodObject`, `getMethodsListWithAnnotation`/`getMethodsWithAnnotation` (2-arg and 4-arg, including `searchSupers`/`ignoreAccess` effects and NPE cases).
- `getOverrideHierarchy`: with `Interfaces.INCLUDE`/`EXCLUDE`/`null`, ordering and NPE on null method.
- `invokeExactMethod`/`invokeExactStaticMethod`: exact-type matching, `NoSuchMethodException` on mismatch, NPE on null object.
- `invokeMethod`/`invokeStaticMethod`: primitive wrapping, `forceAccess`, interface-based accessibility, wrapped `InvocationTargetException`, NPE on null object.

All fixtures (annotations, interfaces, nested classes) are defined inline in the test file, and `./compile.sh` reports success.
